summary: IBM published Granite Speech 5.

title: NVIDIA Kumo Relational predicts from business databases with no training
summary: NVIDIA introduced Kumo Relational, a pre-trained model that makes predictions directly on company databases.

title: Trimming a small model's vocabulary cuts running costs by 77%
summary: Dharma AI describes VocabX, a method for specialising the vocabulary of small language models.

title: OlmoEarth v1.3 maps the whole planet with AI — and you can explore it in your browser
summary: The Allen Institute for AI released OlmoEarth v1.

title: Xbox wants to charge per hour to stream games you already bought
summary: Ars Technica reports that Xbox plans to charge 24 to 40 cents per hour to stream games from the cloud, including games you've already paid for.

title: Quad9 is leaving France
summary: Quad9, a free non-profit service that translates website names into addresses and blocks known malicious sites, announced it is exiting France.

title: eMudhra quits the website certificate business
summary: Previously covered on 2026-10-21: a report described a compromise of one of eMudhra's certificate authorities, the organisations that vouch for websites as secure.

title: Anthropic: AI is making mathematically proven software practical
summary: Anthropic published research arguing that AI models are making formal verification — mathematically proving that software does exactly what it should — feasible at a much larger scale.

title: GitHub has copied 99.99999% of its repositories to Azure
summary: GitHub says it has moved a copy of 99.

title: Rebuilding GitHub's star history: from 2,500 requests to 24
summary: GitHub launched a new API that shows how a project's star count changed over time.

title: Google may use your Gmail and Photos to target ads
summary: The Verge reports that Google has updated its privacy policy, tied to its 'personal intelligence' AI features, to say it might use data from your Gmail and Google Photos to target ads.

title: Anthropic maps out possible futures for an AI economy
summary: Anthropic published 'Scenarios for our economic future', which starts from an honest admission: nobody yet knows how AI will reshape the economy.

title: From a health worker's notebook to an Ebola situation report
summary: Anthropic's feature 'The Situation Report' follows the Ebola response in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, where community health workers record fevers, recoveries and deaths and text their notes over WhatsApp.

title: Kimi releases K3.1 Pro and a faster Highspeed version
summary: Kimi, the AI assistant from Chinese company Moonshot AI, released two new models: K3.

title: LitPivot helps researchers see where their idea fits
summary: The Allen Institute for AI introduced LitPivot, a tool that helps researchers develop ideas by showing them how relevant papers change the picture.

title: Hugging Face lists which models run on AWS Trainium
summary: Previously covered on 2026-10-20: Hugging Face introduced TorchNeuron, a native PyTorch backend for Amazon's Trainium AI chips.

title: Astral brings its uv and ty Python tools together
summary: Astral, the company behind uv (a fast tool for installing Python packages and managing projects) and ty (a tool that checks Python code for type errors before it runs), announced an integration between the two.

title: How much of the creative job slump is AI?
summary: Economics newsletter Apricitas looks at the roughly 200,000 jobs the US has lost in media, film and the arts, and asks how much of that decline AI can actually explain.

title: Terence Tao launches a hub to check OpenAI's math write-ups
summary: Mathematician Terence Tao announced oai-math-revised, a community project where people can review and revise the write-ups OpenAI has published about math results.

title: A security flaw spreads to many web software libraries
summary: Security firm Aikido reports that a vulnerability known as Node2Shell has evolved into HTTP2Shell, and now affects many libraries and apps that handle web traffic, including Python packages.

title: How three Java experts use GitHub Copilot day to day
summary: GitHub asked three Java Champions — recognised experts in the Java programming language — how they use its Copilot AI assistant.

title: Roku moves its developer projects from GitHub to GitLab
summary: Roku says its developer code repositories have moved from GitHub to GitLab, a competing platform.

title: ThinkingBox: training AI agents by checking the database, not their word
summary: Microsoft released ThinkingBox-Training on GitHub, a follow-up to its earlier post 'The Agent Said It Was Done.

title: Cerebras explains how it runs trillion-parameter models
summary: AI chipmaker Cerebras published a write-up on how it deploys frontier AI models with around a trillion parameters — the internal settings a model learns during training — on its own hardware.

title: AI prices have fallen by up to 80% in a few months
summary: Data scientist Max Woolf looks at why OpenAI and Anthropic have cut the prices of their AI models by up to 80% within just a few months.

title: A decade-old specialist AI beats today's chatbots at spotting skin cancer
summary: Researchers report that a 10-year-old image-recognition model built only for skin cancer diagnosis outperforms today's leading general-purpose AI models at the task.

title: IBM's CEO: open AI models are now good and cheap enough to run in-house
summary: IBM's chief executive says open-weight models — AI models that companies can download and run on their own computers — are now 'irresistibly good and cheap' to run on-premises, The Register reports.

title: DreamHost is forcing password resets during an active incident
summary: Web hosting company DreamHost's status page reports an active incident that is forcing customers to reset their passwords.

title: Losing a job to AI costs more than a paycheck
summary: The Economist argues that if AI displaces human workers, they will lose more than just their pay.

title: Reflection releases Beam, a 501-billion-parameter open model
summary: Hugging Face welcomed Beam, a new open model with 501 billion parameters — the internal settings a model learns during training, and a rough measure of its size.

title: The state of context engineering
summary: Writer Drew Breunig surveys the state of context engineering — the practice of carefully choosing what information you feed an AI model alongside your request, so it has exactly what it needs to do the job well.

title: OpenAI reports three new discoveries in maths, computer science and physics
summary: OpenAI published a post describing three new results in mathematics, computer science and physics, built with academic researchers.

title: OpenAI introduces GPT-6.1 Terra
summary: OpenAI announced a new model, GPT-6.

title: Cloudflare's AI service leaked responses between users
summary: Cloudflare disclosed that its Workers AI service exposed parts of some requests to other users when running the GLM-5.

title: Microsoft offers buyouts to about a quarter of its staff
summary: The Seattle Times reports that Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to roughly a quarter of its workforce.

title: Solar power is overtaking nuclear
summary: BBC Future looks at how solar power is becoming a bigger source of electricity than nuclear.

title: Blaze claims Rust builds up to 92x faster
summary: A new open-source project, Blaze, says it makes incremental builds of Rust programs — rebuilding after a small code change — up to 92 times faster than Rust's standard tools, cargo and rustc.

title: Sebastian Raschka's course on building reasoning models from scratch
summary: Machine learning author Sebastian Raschka released a from-scratch video course on building reasoning models — AI models that work through a problem step by step before answering.

title: Liquid AI releases LFM3: one family of small models for text, images and audio
summary: Liquid AI released LFM3, a new generation of its foundation models that puts text, vision, audio, combined 'omni' and decision-making models on one shared base.

title: Anthropic expands deal to bring Claude to all levels of US government
summary: Anthropic is expanding its partnership with the GSA, the US agency that buys goods and services for the federal government, to make Claude available across all levels of government.

title: Google DeepMind unveils Genie 4 for simulating virtual worlds
summary: Google DeepMind introduced Genie 4, a new generation of its world-simulation models — AI that generates interactive environments you can move around in.

title: Anthropic reports early progress using Claude to speed up drug development
summary: Anthropic published research on early results from using Claude to help accelerate the development of new medicines.

title: Firmware flaw puts most of the world's servers at risk
summary: Ars Technica reports a code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware — the low-level software that starts a computer before its operating system loads — that threatens most servers in use today.

title: Can AI judge whether a research idea is actually new?
summary: The Allen Institute for AI released 'Old Ideas, Novel Problems', a study of how reliably large language models can judge the novelty of scientific research ideas.

title: Python's experimental speed-up compiler is being removed
summary: LWN reports that Python's experimental JIT compiler — a feature that translates code into faster machine instructions while a program runs — is set to be removed from the language.

title: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 5.5, at 40% lower cost
summary: Anthropic introduced Claude Opus 5.

title: Google introduces Gemini 4 Carbon
summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon, a new model in its Gemini family, on its official blog.

title: Developers are building with AI agents at record levels
summary: GitHub's 2026 Octoverse report says commits and pushes — the basic units of saving and sharing code — reached new highs this year as developers increasingly work with AI agents.

title: Testing AI agents on 50 real tax assignments
summary: Surge AI published Dayjob: Tax, an evaluation of how well AI agents handle 50 professional tax assignments.

title: GitHub lays out its vision at Universe 2026
summary: At its annual Universe conference, GitHub described its plan to become an end-to-end system for delivering software, from writing code to shipping it.

title: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe: speech-to-text you can steer
summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.

title: Qwenputer: a working computer chip simulated inside an AI model
summary: A developer built Qwenputer, a functioning, deterministic RISC-V CPU — a simple processor design — running inside the Qwen3.
